test: curvo inverse on force-paired real-membrane data

dataset.source: Roy, Steinkühler, Zhao, Lipowsky, Dimova (2020) Nano Lett. 20:3185
dataset.tier: T1 force-paired (super-resolution STED geometry + micropipette-set tension)
dataset.system: POPC GUV, symmetric bilayer, spontaneous curvature ~0

forward_check: curvo helfrich_tube reproduces the system: reported 72 nm tube <-> Sigma ~ 36 uN/m (within the 15-140 range), holding force ~ 16.5 pN

inverse_test.observable: STED tube radius (noise sigma_R = 5.5 nm, half the reported +/-11 nm on diameter)
inverse_test.prior: kappa ~ Normal(23,5) kBT (paper's own tube-pulling uncertainty)
inverse_test.inferred: posterior over membrane tension sigma -> propagated to holding force f
inverse_test.method: exact 2D grid posterior over (sigma, kappa); force posterior by propagation

summary.verdict: ACCEPTABLE — forces recovered near-unbiased (mean |bias| 3.8%) across the paper's full tension range; 68% CIs are conservative (coverage 0.90-0.97), erring toward humility not overconfidence. Mild low-tension positive bias is the sqrt-nonlinearity mapping radius noise asymmetrically to force (explainable, not a defect).

honest_scope: This validates curvo's forward map and Bayesian inverse machinery on the TUBE/tether geometry (helfrich_tube evaluator) against real force-paired data. It is distinct from the CCS spherical-cap analyze() pipeline. It confirms the physics engine + inversion are calibrated on real measured forces; it does not by itself validate the multi-actor CCS decomposition.
